Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

whether … or conjunction

also whether or not, … or not, either way

classical

Varr. RR 3.2.11: quid enim rēfert, utrum propter ovēs, an propter avēs frūctūs capiās?
Plaut. Pers. 3.1.13: utrum prō ancillā mē habēs, an prō fīliā? (Lewis & Short)

utrum … an

conjunctions: an alternative question, direct, or indirect with the subjunctive; utrum may be left out

Also -ne … an and plain … an. “Or not” is necne in an indirect question, annōn in a direct one.

Other words

  • -ne … an — whether … or

    enclitic on the first word, an before the second · also used · classical · Tac. Germ. 5.3: argentum et aurum propitiīne an īrātī diī negāverint dubitō

  • necne — or not

    conjunction, at the end of an indirect question · also used · classical · Ter. Heaut. 1.1.43: nunc habeam necne, incertum est (Lewis & Short)

    In a direct question, annōn: Tibi ego dīcō, annōn? (Ter. And. 762).

  • sīve … sīve (seu … seu) — whether … or (either way)

    conjunctions, with the moods of sī · also used · classical · Phaedr. 4.22.7–8: sīve hoc ineptum sīve laudandum est opus

    Not a question but a double condition: “whether it is this or that, the main clause holds”.

Examples

  • quid enim rēfert, utrum propter ovēs, an propter avēs frūctūs capiās?

    for what does it matter whether you make your profit from sheep or from birds?Varr. RR 3.2.11

  • utrum prō ancillā mē habēs, an prō fīliā?

    do you take me for a servant girl, or for your daughter?Plaut. Pers. 3.1.13 (Lewis & Short)

  • argentum et aurum propitiīne an īrātī diī negāverint dubitō

    whether the gods denied them silver and gold in kindness or in anger, I cannot tellTac. Germ. 5.3

  • Amīcum an nōmen habeās, aperit calamitās.

    Misfortune shows whether you have a friend or only the name of one.Publ. A 42

  • Tibi ego dīcō, annōn?

    Am I talking to you or not?Ter. And. 762

  • sīve Aquilō rādit terrās seu brūma nivālem interiōre diem gȳrō trahit, īre necesse est

    whether the north wind scours the land or midwinter drags the snowy day round its shorter circle, I have to goHor. S. 2.6.25–26

See also whether, or, either … or.
